Status epilepticus (SE) – a seizure lasting ≥5 min or recurrent seizures without full recovery of consciousness between episodes.
Failure of termination mechanisms (e.g., exhausted inhibitory interneurons) → prolonged seizure activity → status epilepticus.
Critical: Multi‑organ failure, shock, severe haemolysis, status epilepticus — Emergency resuscitation, multidisciplinary team, possible transfer to tertiary centre

qs.q: Which cytokine biomarker ratio is predictive of hippocampal abnormalities on MRI after febrile status epilepticus?
qs.e: A decreased ILR-1A/IL-8 ratio suggests an overall proinflammatory state and is predictive of hippocampal abnormalities on MRI done after febrile status epilepticus. This ratio may serve as a potential biomarker for future mesial temporal lobe epilepsy risk.

qs.q: Children presenting with febrile status epilepticus are most frequently found to have infections caused by which organisms?
qs.e: In patients presenting with febrile status epilepticus, HHV-6B and HHV-7 infections account for 30% of the cases. Febrile seizures overall can occur with various infections such as otitis media or roseola.

qs.q: Which cytokine alteration is associated with febrile status epilepticus and a potential risk for mesial temporal lobe epilepsy?
o: An elevated ILR-1A/IL-8 ratio indicating an anti-inflammatory state
A decreased ILR-1A/IL-8 ratio suggestive of an overall proinflammatory state
Complete absence of interleukin-6 in cerebrospinal fluid
Overexpression of anti-inflammatory IL-1beta cytokines exclusively
qs.e: A decreased ILR-1A/IL-8 ratio suggests an overall proinflammatory state and is predictive of hippocampal abnormalities on MRI after febrile status epilepticus. This ratio serves as a potential biomarker for identifying patients at higher risk for mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.

qs.q: How should cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings be interpreted when a lumbar puncture is performed in a patient presenting with febrile status epilepticus?
o: Pleocytosis is universally present in over 90% of uncomplicated cases.
A nontraumatic lumbar puncture rarely shows pleocytosis, with 96% having under 3 cells.
Elevated CSF protein and glucose levels are required to confirm a viral etiology.
CSF findings will always show a marked decrease in glucose due to consumption.
qs.e: In patients with febrile status epilepticus, a nontraumatic lumbar puncture rarely shows CSF pleocytosis, with 96% having fewer than 3 nucleated cells and concurrently normal protein and glucose. Any significant pleocytosis should raise suspicion for a bacterial or viral CNS infection.

qs.q: Which viral infections are frequently noted in the context of febrile seizures and account for approximately 30% of cases presenting as febrile status epilepticus?
o: Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
qs.e: Febrile seizures frequently occur in the context of HHV-6 infections, and in patients presenting specifically with febrile status epilepticus, HHV-6B and HHV-7 account for 30% of the cases. Other common triggers include otitis media and enteroviruses.

qs.q: What is the ILAE-defined threshold time (t1) to initiate treatment for generalized tonic-clonic status epilepticus?
qs.e: For generalized tonic-clonic seizures, status epilepticus is defined with t1 equal to 5 minutes to prompt early treatment. A 30-minute cut-off was historically used based on animal studies showing neuronal damage, but this has been reduced.

qs.q: What is the defining threshold time (t1) for initiating treatment in focal status epilepticus with impaired awareness?
qs.e: Focal status epilepticus with impaired awareness has a defined treatment initiation threshold (t1) of 10 minutes. This contrasts with generalized tonic-clonic seizures which have a t1 of 5 minutes.
qs.s: Acute management of seizure and status epilepticus: MCQs

qs.q: In which age group is status epilepticus most frequently observed?
qs.e: Status epilepticus is most common in children younger than 5 years of age, with an incidence of over 100 per 100,000 in this group. Febrile status epilepticus is also the most common type of status epilepticus in children.
